result.title: ORDO: Operation-level Round-aware Dynamic Ordering for MIP Presolve
result.summary: Presolve strongly affects mixed-integer programming (MIP) performance, yet learning-based methods only optimize parameter configurations and cannot express the non-commutative temporal dependencies among actions, whose default order is nearly unique on most domains, yet functionally necessary: artificially shuffling the order of the same sequence inflates the tail of the solve-time distribution by up to several-fold. We recast presolve planning as autoregressive sequence generation over a unified atomic action space, moving the decision object to action sequences; we call this framework ORDO---Operation-level Round-aware Dynamic Ordering for MIP Presolve. Its payoff is cross-domain generalization: on multiple unseen domains it attains end-to-end zero-shot speedup---to our knowledge the first for presolve action sequences---varying by domain and not explained by corpus richness, the strongest domain reaching the largest speedup once racing is added. Deployment uses sequence racing, in which candidate sequences run concurrently and the winner is kept, enabled by an execution-and-observation facility, added by modifying the SCIP source, that injects sequences along the native path and records which actions actually execute and in which round.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将 MIP presolve 规划重构为统一原子动作空间上的自回归序列生成（ORDO），并借助改造 SCIP 得到的执行—观测设施，用序列 racing 并行运行候选序列、保留胜者，实现跨域零样本加速。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把决策对象移到动作序列、显式建模非交换时序依赖，以及并行候选序列 racing 后保留胜者的做法，可能为 LVR 中推理状态的生成顺序、并行候选生成与验证选择提供方法线索，可供核查。
